chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Faḍālah, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Maysarah, who said:

I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say, concerning a man who saw something after ghusl: He said, “If he had urinated after his intercourse before the ghusl, then let him perform wudu (ablution); and if he had not urinated until he performed ghusl, then afterward found moisture, let him repeat the ghusl.”

As for what these two hadiths contain regarding the mention of repeating wudu (ablution), that is only by way of recommendation, because when it is established by what we mentioned earlier that ghusl from janabah suffices in place of wudu (ablution), and nothing has occurred here that nullifies wudu (ablution), then it should not be obligatory upon him to repeat the taharah, and taharah is not binding upon his liability except with decisive proof. And there is no proof here that removes the excuse. It is also possible that what came out from him after the ghusl was urine, in which case wudu (ablution) would then be obligatory upon him, even if ghusl were not obligatory, according to what the report indicates.

key_terms.الطَّهَارَةِ: ritual purity required for acts of worship
key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation rather than obligation in legal application
key_terms.الْبَلَلَ: moisture or wetness later found after ghusl
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: state of major ritual impurity caused here by intercourse
key_terms.الْخَبَرُ: the report or hadith being cited as legal evidence
key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: ritual bath, specifically ghusl from janabah
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: ritual ablution performed for prayer and other acts requiring purity
key_terms.جِمَاعِهِ: his sexual intercourse, the cause of janabah in this context

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone finds moisture after ghusl from janabah?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on finding moisture after ghusl from janabah and distinguishes between the cases of having urinated before ghusl or not. The accompanying explanation states that repeating wudu (ablution) is understood as recommended unless there is clear proof of a nullifying event, while repeating ghusl may be required if the discharged moisture is treated as remaining seminal fluid.
